post_text:
10 days. 10 government datasets. 10 findings.
Every number on a website you can open right now.
Zero paywalls. Zero FOIA requests.

The data was always there.

Mississippi leads national reading improvement because of a curriculum decision made in 2013 — a decade before most states caught up. Cleveland cut absenteeism while Memphis added 9.6 points — same ESSER funding, different intervention model. Utah gets 3.6x more reading proficiency per dollar than New York. None of these findings required proprietary data. They required someone to connect the spreadsheets.

---

→ 10 original findings — one per day, each sourced to a live government database with clickable links
→ All 10 interactive dashboards — live on GitHub Pages, all code public
→ Methodology section — 4 design principles applied consistently across every day
→ Author contact — open to applying this kind of analysis to real education data questions

Day 10 of 10 · Challenge complete · From Memphis to 50 States
Data: TDOE · Census ACS · FutureEd · NCES · NAEP · EDFacts · Urban Institute — all free
One analyst. One laptop. Ten government spreadsheets. This is what synthesis looks like.

📊 Full interactive dashboard → link in first comment 👇
